items.label: Supermicro Q4 FY2026 (08-11-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Q4 FY2026 (ended 06-30-2026) revenue $11.1B, +93% YoY and +9% QoQ, nea

set.signal: Q4 FY2026 revenue $11.1B, +93% YoY and +9% QoQ, near the low end of the $11 billion-$12.5 billion guide due to delays in customer readiness (CEO: 'short-term customer delay in power shortage, cooling, and networking'); CFO: that revenue is anticipated to be recognized in subsequent quarters. Non-GAAP gross margin 17.6% vs 8.2-8.4% guided and 10.1% in Q3 (+750bps QoQ) - CFO: ~75% of the improvement from a better than anticipated customer and product mix 'including the deferral of several contracts from Q4 fiscal year 2026 to Q1 fiscal year 2027, and perhaps the subsequent quarter', ~25% from lower tariff costs and lower inventory reserves (no tariff rebate booked). Non-GAAP operating margin 14.3% (vs 7.2% in Q3); non-GAAP EPS $1.70 (GAAP $1.62) vs $0.65-0.79 guided. Full-year FY2026 revenue $39.1B, up 78% over FY2025 ($22 billion); FY2026 non-GAAP EPS $3.63 (+76% vs $2.06); FY2026 non-GAAP gross margin 10.9% (vs 11.2%) and non-GAAP operating margin 8.1% (vs 7.1%). Over $60B of NEW ORDERS received in Q4 drove backlog to a record. Guidance: Q1 FY2027 revenue $14.5-15.5B, gross margin 10.4-10.8%, non-GAAP EPS $1.01-1.10; FY2027 revenue $65-72B.

items.reason: Restores the CFO's hedge on the deferred contracts ('and perhaps the subsequent quarter') and uses the stated numbers ($11 billion, $22 billion) instead of reformatted ones. Verifier: the quarter-end date (06-30-2026) is not stated on the call and is dropped.
items.evidence: including the deferral of several contracts from Q4 fiscal year 2026 to Q1 fiscal year 2027, and perhaps the subsequent quarter.

items.label: Supermicro Q4 FY2026 (08-11-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Deployment timing, not demand, is the constraint: Q4 revenue of $11.1B

set.signal: Deployment timing, not demand, is the constraint: CEO Charles Liang says Q4 revenue of $11.1B came in 'due to some short-term customer delay in power shortage, cooling, and networking', 'purely a timing story', with the revenue anticipated in subsequent quarters (CFO); OEM appliance / large-datacenter revenue fell 26% QoQ to $5.5B while enterprise/channel rose 98% QoQ. CEO: 'Large data center always have power readiness, data center readiness concern, especially liquid cooling', yet order and shipment for the September and December quarters 'have been quite strong'. On OEM versus ODM: 'We have an OEM business, but we also cover ODM business... We will continue to grow in both ways.' DCBBS is pitched as the answer to the readiness problem - a turnkey ecosystem (direct liquid cooling, CDU, chill door, water tower, high-speed switch and networking, management software, lifecycle services) that lets customers build and scale AI data centers in quarters rather than years and improves time-to-deployment (TTD) and time-to-online (TTO).

items.reason: The call does not say the delayed customers were Neoclouds, and the ODM-disintermediation framing was the analyst's; replaced with the CEO's own words.
items.evidence: We have an OEM business, but we also cover ODM business. We have lots of large data center customer now, especially a kind of Neocloud.

items.label: Supermicro Q4 FY2026 (08-11-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Networking is now an explicit DCBBS pillar: the total solution spans C

set.signal: Networking is now an explicit DCBBS pillar: the total solution spans CPU and GPU compute, storage, energy and a 1.6T HIGH-SPEED SWITCH plus 'upcoming optical networking', sold with the Supermicro management software suite (SCM, SuperCloud Composer, SVM, SOM). The new 32-acre Silicon Valley DCBBS campus features an ADVANCED OPTICAL PHOTONICS NETWORKING LAB alongside datacenter-scale manufacturing, and CEO Charles Liang calls out the high-speed switch and optical technology as areas of very aggressive continued investment, citing 'a high bandwidth switch and the whole networking design management tool' as a big room to grow for DCBBS. Customer networking readiness (alongside power and cooling) was one of the causes of the Q4 revenue push-out.

items.reason: The '~20%-of-gross-profit DCBBS target' was the analyst's framing in the question, not management's statement.
items.evidence: So, we see a very big room to grow, including a kind of a switch, a high bandwidth switch and the whole networking design management tool.

items.label: Supermicro Q4 FY2026 (08-11-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Power and cooling readiness at the CUSTOMER site was the direct cause

set.signal: Power and cooling readiness at the CUSTOMER site was the direct cause of the Q4 revenue shortfall - CEO Charles Liang: Q4 revenue came in at $11.1 billion 'due to some short-term customer delay in power shortage, cooling, and networking'. DCBBS is the response: a turnkey stack of direct liquid cooling solutions, CDU, chill door, water tower, high-speed data switch and networking, Supermicro Data Center Management software (SCM, SuperCloud Composer, SVM, SOM Orchestration Manager) and full lifecycle services, plus a new PROACTIVE SERVICE model (a proactive service package earlier next quarter) where management software and field teams automatically alert and are ready to fix failed units, preventing loss of compute capacity. On DCBBS's share of gross profit, the CEO said '20% should be not far away.' Liquid cooling penetration keeps rising - GPU and CPU platforms alike (Vera, Rubin) are liquid-cooling-ready and the CEO believes liquid cooling 'very soon will dominate the data center business'.
set.figure: Q4 miss on customer power/cooling/networking readiness; CEO on DCBBS: '20% should be not far away'

items.reason: 'Power shelves/battery backup' is not in the call, and 'previously guided to ~20% of gross profit' was the analyst's statement; only the CEO's '20% should be not far away' is management's.
items.evidence: So, we see a big room to grow. 20% should be not far away.
